questions_and_answers.question_text: What does hǎo mean in the phrase hǎo jiǔ?
How does the verb jiàn differ from kànjian?
What is the literal meaning of chū mén?
With which kind of action is yòu used?
Write the Chinese for "I haven't seen you for a long time."
Give three examples of hǎo meaning "very."

answers.answer_text: Hǎo dà ("very large"), hǎo duō rén ("a good many people"), hǎo jǐtian ("quite a few days").

questions_and_answers.question_text: What do Běijīng speakers think of the Taiwanese Hǎo hǎochī!?

answers.answer_text: They think that this repetition of hǎo sounds bad.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Oh, you have come again!"
Write the Chinese for "Yes, I went to Guǎngzhōu again."

answers.answer_text: Shì a, wǒ yòu dào Guǎngzhōu qu le.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which verb would you use for "to perceive an object"?

articles.text:
1. B: Hǎo jiǔ méi jiàn, nín chū     I haven't seen you for a long time.
      mén le ba?                      You have been away, I suppose?
   A: Shì a, wǒ yòu dào Guǎngzhōu    Yes, I went to Guǎngzhōu again.
      qu le.

Notes on No. 1

Hǎo jiǔ, "very long": In this phrase, the word hǎo means "very." Some additional examples of this use of hǎo are

hǎo dà                           very large
hǎo duō rén                      a good many people
hǎo jǐtian                       quite a few days

Persons from Taiwan frequently use hǎo, "very," before another hǎo, as in Hǎo hǎowán! "What fun!" and Hǎo hǎochī! "Delicious!" Speakers from Běijīng think that this repetition of hǎo sounds bad.

The verb jiàn means "to see someone" in the sense of "to visit/talk with someone." The verb kànjian is used for "to see" in the sense of "to perceive an object."

Chū mén means "to go out," "to go away from home," "to go out of town"; literally, "to go out the door."

Yòu is the word for "again" which is used with completed actions.

Ou, nǐ yòu lái le!               Oh, you have come again!
Qìshuǐ yòu méiyou le.            We are out of soda again.
Tā zuótian méi shàng kè.         Yesterday he didn't attend class.
Jīntian yòu méi shàng kè.        Today, again, he didn't attend class.
